legend.text: One note per data sample, about every two seconds. Higher note means a warmer ocean on average.
More ocean above 28 degrees: the note repeats faster, up to four times.
Hotter hot spots: the notes get louder and brighter.
The sound leans right when the northern oceans are warmer, left when the southern oceans are.
A soft bell marks each new month.

mappings.label: Mean sea temperature
mappings.why: Colour → pitch. Area-weighted mean of the decoded °C values: warmer ocean = higher note. The year's small swing (about 19.5–20.2 °C) is stretched across the pitch range so it is audible; the quiet guide tone follows the exact value.

mappings.label: Ocean ≥ 28 °C
mappings.why: Share of decoded ocean at or above 28 °C (the tropical warm pool): more warm water = the note repeats more often (1 to 4 times per sample).

mappings.label: Warmest 10 % of the ocean
mappings.why: 90th percentile of decoded temperature: hotter hot spots = louder, brighter notes (3 loudness steps).

mappings.label: North − south mid-latitudes
mappings.why: Northern minus southern mid-latitude temperature (30–60°): northern summer leans right, southern summer leans left.
